title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
excerpt: Multi-agent systems often rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their ability to adapt to diverse task requirements. We introduce DynaFlow, a framework that integrates free-form executable workflow synthesis into the action space of the main agent. The agent decides when collaboration is needed and generates task-specific programs that coordinate sub-agents through sequential or parallel execution, structured information exchange, and verification. Execution results and traces inform subsequent actions, enabling the agent to adapt collaboration as reasoning progresses. We train only the main agent through supervised fine-tuning on distilled trajectories, followed by…

ai.summary: DynaFlow adds free‑form executable workflow synthesis to an agent's action space, letting it generate programs that coordinate sub‑agents dynamically.
ai.why: Allows developers to build more adaptable multi‑agent systems that can create custom collaboration scripts on the fly.

title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
excerpt: People have long dreamed of an assistant that is always there to guide them and remind what they forget, from new dishes to lost keys. Powered by multimodal large language models (MLLMs), egocentric AI assistants on wearable devices are bringing this dream within reach: they see what the user sees and give instructions for user's physical work when necessary. However, testing such assistance is challenging and usually requires real people. The expensive and rare real interaction data leaves a key question unanswered: Can today's MLLMs truly help people in physical world? To answer this question, we propose InteractiveWorld, the first verifiable environment for closed-loop interaction…

ai.summary: InteractiveWorld presents a verifiable, human‑centric simulation environment for testing multimodal LLM assistants in egocentric scenarios.
ai.why: Offers a low‑cost, reproducible platform for developers to evaluate and improve wearable AI assistants.

title: World-in-Context: Interactive Video World Modeling with In-Context Conditioning
excerpt: Interactive video world models require coordinated control over viewing perspectives, character actions, and camera motion. Existing methods typically leave view modes implicit in text captions, conflate action with camera motion, and inject controls through fragmented architectural pathways that capture interdependencies only indirectly. In this work, we present World-in-Context, an interactive world modeling framework powered by In-Context Conditioning (ICC). Rather than relying on specialized conditioning pathways, World-in-Context unifies view, action, and camera controls into explicit tokens contextualized directly within a shared self-attention space. Our formulation reveals that (i)…

ai.summary: World‑in‑Context delivers an interactive video world‑modeling framework that uses in‑context conditioning to jointly control viewpoint, character actions, and camera motion.
ai.why: Gives developers a unified approach to generate and manipulate interactive video scenes with coherent control signals.

title: Principia: Test-Time Hypotheses to Principle Construction for Scientific Discovery
excerpt: Scientific discovery requires identifying the scientific principles underlying observed phenomena to guide further investigation. As these empirical principles are often unknown in complex discovery processes, they are constructed via a hypotheses-to-principle pipeline to obtain recurring causalities from progressively accumulated observations during test-time discovery. However, constructing this knowledge requires substantial domain expertise, time, and effort, making this translation stage a bottleneck for scientific discovery. To address this limitation, we propose Principia, an LLM-based framework that constructs and continually refines scientific principles at test time. Drawing on…

ai.summary: Principia proposes a test‑time hypotheses‑to‑principle pipeline that constructs scientific principles from accumulated observations to guide discovery without extensive domain expertise.
ai.why: Provides a framework developers can integrate into AI‑driven scientific workflows to automate hypothesis generation and principle extraction.

title: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution
excerpt: LLM agents are increasingly used to solve real-world problems, and their effectiveness depends on both the underlying models and the harnesses that support their operation. However, most existing benchmarks focus on model capabilities and overall agent performance, with limited attention to the evaluation of agent harnesses. To address this gap, we introduce TraceTrial-Bench, which organizes harness reliability into seven components covering context, execution, governance, lifecycle, observability, tools, and verification. We construct 95 expert-level, mechanism-oriented tasks with executable or state-based ground truth to support semantically equivalent comparisons while preserving the…

ai.summary: TraceTrial‑Bench is a benchmark that evaluates the reliability of LLM agent harnesses across seven components such as context handling and observability.
ai.why: Helps developers identify and fix weak points in the infrastructure that supports LLM agents.

title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
excerpt: Successful tool-use trajectories are not necessarily useful supervision. Even successful interactions may underrepresent multi-step dependencies or contain actions that are unjustified by the information visible to the agent at decision time. We identify two coupled requirements for effective trajectory supervision: compositional coverage, so that important observation-action dependencies are represented, and decision grounding, so that each supervised action is supported by the learner-visible interaction history. We introduce Trajectory2Gym, which constructs executable interactions around under-supported compositional structures and derives supervision only from grounded decisions in…

ai.summary: Trajectory2Gym introduces a framework that generates tool-use trajectories with compositional coverage and decision grounding to better supervise agents.
ai.why: It provides higher-quality training data for tool-use agents, improving multi-step reasoning and action justification.

title: How AI agents shape experts’ judgment calls
excerpt: As AI does more of the hands-on work, the hope is that experts still make the judgment calls, meaning the decisions with more than one defensible answer. We tested this with 50 professional analysts who did a statistical analysis with Claude Code. On each key decision, we randomly assigned which of two defensible options the agent would favor. Analysts mostly went with the agent’s side, and few named the agent as a reason afterward.

ai.summary: A study with 50 professional analysts showed that when Claude Code suggested one of two defensible options in statistical analyses, analysts tended to follow the AI’s recommendation, rarely citing the model as the reason.

title: Representation Redistribution in Sparse Autoencoders
excerpt: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose language model activations into sparse features, but prompt transformations designed to preserve the underlying request can redistribute activity across them. A feature change observed on one transformed prompt need not recur, and even a recurring change need not affect a downstream computation. We introduce the redistribution sensitivity score (RSS), which identifies large feature responses that recur in a consistent direction, and evaluate the resulting supports on variants excluded from selection. Across 27 pretrained SAEs spanning eight language models, the tested prompt transformations produce a reproducible redistribution profile on these excluded…

ai.summary: The authors introduce the Redistribution Sensitivity Score (RSS) to measure how prompt transformations shift activity across sparse autoencoder features, identifying stable feature changes that consistently affect downstream computations.
ai.why: Helps developers interpret and control sparse representations in language models for more reliable prompting.

title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
excerpt: Vision-language models are shifting from offline passive understanding toward online proactive interaction. However, prevailing methods largely rely on explicit requests while miss the implicit user intent (e.g., "where should I click next?" while a user navigate a website), meanwhile fail to update the state simultaneously as user requests might update continuously. These limitations make them less suited to intent-aware interaction in practical. To address these challenges, we introduce StreamVibe-Bench, a new benchmark serving as testbed for user intent interaction, with 4.1K evaluation samples and 85K training samples spanning explicit, implicit, and dynamic intents. Building on this…

ai.summary: StreamVibe proposes proactive video agents that infer implicit user intent and continuously update state to interact with evolving user requests.
ai.why: Enables developers to build more responsive video-based assistants that anticipate actions without explicit prompts.

title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
excerpt: AI systems built around large models increasingly use experience and feedback to make persistent changes to models, prompts, memories, tools, and workflows. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) extends this process to inductive biases and to the mechanisms that govern future updates, which can themselves be revised and reused across improvement cycles. Yet self-modification alone does not guarantee trustworthy improvement. Reported gains may reflect flawed evaluations, previously acquired capabilities may deteriorate, and compliance with behavioral constraints may weaken. Compromised artifacts or sensitive information may also persist in successor systems. Changes to improvement mechanisms may…

ai.summary: The report surveys recursive self‑improvement (RSI) for large models, outlining foundations, risks, evaluation methods, and open challenges for trustworthy self‑modifying AI systems.

We introduce two complementary dimensions, work persistence and work openness, to characterize working conditions, and classify digital work into five forms according to task…

ai.summary: Work Agents paper frames agents as systems that combine foundation models with runtime harnesses to execute tasks in stateful workspaces, proposing a unified perspective on work‑centric agent design and optimization.

title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
excerpt: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as the primary paradigm for optimizing Large Language Model (LLM) agents, yet efficient critic-free algorithms (e.g., GRPO) suffer from a fundamental uniform credit assignment dilemma that broadcasts trajectory-level advantages equally to all actions. Our analysis reveals that this uniformity inherently reinforces structurally unreasonable actions in preferred trajectories and ignores each action's downstream deviations in unpreferred ones. To resolve this without introducing critic overhead, we propose Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping (ProAS), a plug-and-play framework that leverages a dynamically evolving Agentic Reference Graph (ARG) to achieve…

ai.summary: ProAS introduces a Progress‑Aware Advantage Shaping framework that assigns non‑uniform advantages to actions in multi‑turn LLM RL, addressing credit‑assignment issues in critic‑free algorithms like GRPO.
ai.why: Enables developers to train more efficient LLM agents with better credit assignment, improving performance on sequential tasks.

title: Qwen-Image-PE: Learning Visual Design for Text-to-Image Prompt Enhancement
excerpt: Learning visual design is essential for prompt enhancement (PE) to turn underspecified user requests into coherent visual specifications for text-to-image (T2I) generation. Existing methods preserve user intent and improve overall visual appeal, with less explicit emphasis on fine-grained design dimensions. To address this gap, we introduce Qwen-Image-PE, which learns visual design through two-stage training. Supervised fine-tuning with Caption-Based Reverse Distillation (CRD) uses dense captions of well-designed images as design supervision. Reinforcement learning with Groupwise Design Reward (GDR) jointly compares all candidate images for the same request to refine lighting, composition…

ai.summary: Qwen-Image-PE introduces a two-stage training method, including Caption-Based Reverse Distillation, to enhance text-to-image prompts by learning visual design and producing more coherent visual specifications.
ai.why: It offers developers a way to improve prompt quality for T2I models, potentially yielding higher-fidelity images with less manual tweaking.

title: AV-FABLE: Audio-Visual Manipulation Forensics in Long-Form Videos
excerpt: Localized AI manipulations in long-form videos often affect brief events within otherwise authentic content, making video-level classification insufficient for forensic analysis. Existing audio-visual deepfake benchmarks largely focus on short talking-head clips, while long-form temporal forensics remains predominantly visual. We introduce AV-FABLE, a dual-timeline benchmark for sparse manipulations in open-scene long-form audio-visual videos. AV-FABLE contains 16,650 pristine--manipulated twin pairs (998 hours) created with 27 editing configurations, with separate audio and visual timelines that enable modality-specific temporal localization and expose errors hidden by joint-timeline…

ai.summary: AV‑FABLE is a new benchmark containing 16,650 pristine‑manipulated video pairs for detecting sparse audio‑visual forgeries in long‑form content.
ai.why: Provides a large‑scale dataset for improving forensic detection of deepfakes in extended videos.

title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
excerpt: Rubric-based rewards enable effective reinforcement learning on non-verifiable tasks. However, because these rewards are typically defined as a weighted measure of rubric coverage, models are trained primarily to maximize a recall objective. As a result, RL-trained models produce responses that are more complete but also more verbose and contain more unnecessary or factually incorrect content, leading them to be less preferred than responses from the base model. To address this issue, we present the FORK reward, which jointly optimizes recall and a novel precision objective, which requires each unit of a model response to be both necessary and factually correct, as measured by rubric-driven…

ai.summary: The paper presents a precision objective that penalizes unnecessary or incorrect content in rubric‑based RL, reducing reward hacking and improving response quality over standard recall‑focused rewards.
ai.why: Developers can adopt this objective to train LLMs that follow detailed rubrics without becoming overly verbose or hallucinating.

title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
excerpt: Continual learning is the ability of LLM agents to improve over time by acquiring, refining, and applying knowledge from experience while retaining useful prior knowledge. It is essential for agents learning over long time horizons, yet current evaluations largely assess individual task performance rather than improvement through accumulated experience. We introduce Continual Learning Exam (CLE), a large-scale benchmark developed by 50+ domain experts to measure experience-driven improvement in realistic professional workflows. CLE comprises 120 human-authored tasks, each organised as a five-level ladder, yielding 600 levels spanning 89 professional roles across 12 occupational domains…

ai.summary: Continual Learning Exam (CLE) is a benchmark created by 50+ experts to measure LLM agents' ability to improve over time through experience while retaining prior knowledge across long horizons.

excerpt: In this paper, we introduce Δτ-Bench, an executable agent benchmark that models the structural evolution of large tool ecosystems. Against this moving capability frontier, we evaluate whether agents can proactively discover efficient tool-use paths and promptly revise their accumulated procedural knowledge, bringing together demands that existing benchmarks fail to examine. Δτ-Bench comprises 1,588 validated multi-turn tasks across 42 domains and six…

title: HiP3R: Hierarchical Pose Graphs for Long-Horizon 3D Reconstruction
excerpt: Feed-forward models accurately estimate camera motion and 3D geometry from short video windows. However, computational and memory costs prevent direct inference on sequences containing thousands of frames. Long videos must therefore be processed as overlapping chunks. This division produces independent local reconstructions with inconsistent coordinate frames and duplicate estimates of shared cameras. Achieving global consistency requires propagating constraints from adjacent overlaps and distant revisits across the sequence. This requirement naturally motivates pose graph optimization. However, the choice of graph level creates a trade-off. Chunk-level graphs efficiently resolve scale…

ai.summary: The HiP3R paper introduces Hierarchical Pose Graphs, a method that maintains global consistency in long‑horizon 3D reconstruction by propagating constraints across overlapping video chunks.
ai.why: Developers of SLAM and AR applications can adopt HiP3R to reduce memory usage while preserving accurate large‑scale scene geometry.

title: Spatial Audio Generation and Editing with Executable Plans and Self-Distilling Transfusion
excerpt: Spatial audio authoring coordinates source decisions with soundfield synthesis. For editing, plans specify what to change and retain, while reference audio supplies further acoustic detail. First, a shared Transfusion backbone couples autoregressive planning with rectified-flow rendering through executable ScenePlans that specify source content, activity, and 3D trajectories. For editing, the plan describes the full target scene, including retained sources; contrastive features ground the requested change, while full reference latents supply residual…

ai.summary: The paper introduces AMBIT, a framework that uses a Transfusion backbone to generate and edit First‑Order Ambisonics (FOA) spatial audio via executable ScenePlans that specify source content and activity.

Science has a spam problem. And the spam filter is getting clogged up.
According to all reports, academic publishing is drowning in what has come to be called AI slop: low-quality, mass-produced content generated with AI. By 2025, an estimated 57 percent of all published academic articles exhibited detectable evidence of large language model (LLM) influence, a massive jump from 12 percent in 2023. What’s more, over 12 percent of Nature Communications reviews were found to be completely AI-generated in 2025.
Given that for every 40 papers showing statistical evidence of AI usage in 2025, only one formally disclosed it , these figures likely grossly underestimate LLM involvement today. Of…

title: Your Robot’s Safety Functions Already Work. What If the Input Lies?
excerpt:
This article is brought to you by VicOne .
A mobile robot slows for someone in a hallway. A collaborative arm eases its movement as a worker approaches. A humanoid pauses to let a person pass. Each response depends on information about the robot or its surroundings: a distance reading, a position estimate, or a stop signal.
But what happens when one of those inputs is wrong, and the robot still responds exactly as designed? The mobile robot reads the hallway as clear while someone is still there. The arm estimates that the worker is farther away. The humanoid does not receive a stop signal as a person crosses its path.
In each case, a fault could cause that mismatch. So could deliberate…

ai.summary: An IEEE Spectrum article discusses how robots that rely on safety inputs (distance sensors, position estimates, stop signals) can still behave as designed if those inputs are wrong, leading to unsafe behavior.
ai.why: Highlights the need for robust input validation and fault tolerance in robotic safety systems.
